Subject: POC: hands-on workshop runbook & stress session

Hi Simon and team,

Thanks again for the quick intro call yesterday. As discussed, we want to run a hands-on POC kickoff that combines: a prompt & routing review, a short workshop on our routing/caching knobs, and an end-to-end load/benchmark run so we can validate throughput/latency for your expected workload.

High-level goals for the session:
- Walk through sample prompts and routing logic (10–20 minutes)
- Validate throughput targets under realistic prompt mixes (locally simulated)
- Run a controlled benchmark to measure p95/p99 latency and steady-state throughput
- Deliver a short runbook with recommended batching/quantization/routing settings

Target success criteria (for discussion):
- Sustained throughput: ~4k tokens/sec aggregate (demo target)
- Latency: p95 < 350ms for 128-token responses when burst controlled
- Clear list of model variants and config for your staging env

Can you propose 2x 2-hour windows next week that work for your engineers? We suggest blocks that include overlap across PST and CET for broader team attendance; our preference is morning PST (09:00–12:00) to catch east coast folks mid-day.

We will prep a short runbook and a sample Locust harness; if you can share a small set of representative prompts and a staging endpoint (or allow us to connect to a staging host), we can pre-stage the test harness.

Thanks — I can coordinate calendar invites once we lock a slot.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
